newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures recovered after stronger-than-expected U.S. economic figures to settle in the black but traders and analysts said the risks of a decline were mounting.

Traders and analysts said the 5.6 percent rise in U.S. first quarter GDP, and a climb in the implicit price deflator should have more than offset the weak U.S. numbers released on Tuesday but the market clung onto yesterday's gains.
"I'm very surprised by the lack of selling, it's unbelievable. That's a big number and as for the deflator...we just can't understand it," a trader at a French bank said.

"GDP should be more important than earnings. You end up concluding the Fed should hike. Yesterday you thought perhaps they wouldn't - now it's a question of how much," Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro Finance said.
One trader said the French bond reaction was clearly linked to the fact U.S. bonds managed to shrug off the GDP numbers, but he said he would be cautious ahead of U.S. jobs data out Friday.
Another trader said the French market was crying out to be sold but people kept getting caught out by rallies in other markets. "You have to go with the flow," he said.

Traders said on the face of it the OAT sale earlier on Wednesday had good interest, the overall bid to cover ratio was 2.5, but demand for the 2007 was boosted by bids for eight billion francs from one primary dealer. It received 5.3 billion.

A bond salesman at a French bank said there had been some interest from non-residents early on Tuesday although the large bid was probably from a domestic end investor. A trader at another French bank said the majority of their bids at the auction had been from overseas accounts.
Analysts also said were surprised by the fact the French market appeared unconcerned about the upcoming election.

"I still belive the market is much to sanguine about it. The market does not believe the left can win," Brossard said. "The odds for the Socialists are getting close to 50/50 and the trend is clearly down for majority. If it continues... polls should soon turn positive for the Socialists."
"People saw the poll in Le Figaro on Monday and stopped worrying. I don't think they properly appreciate the risk," the salesman said.
The Sofres poll in Le Figaro gave the centre-right ruling coalition a 104 seat majority over the Socialists and Communists.
A CSA poll published on Tuesday put the gap at 38 seats, down from 111 in its poll conducted on April 22, the day after the snap election was called.
The short end of the curve climbed on Wednesday, helped by the strength of the franc, which in turn was boosted by mark weakness against the dollar.
June PIBOR settled up four basis points at 96.42, narrowing the gap over June Euromarks to 34 basis points from well over 40 a week ago.
The franc touched a high of 3.3698 and was trading at 3.3703 at 1515 GMT.
